title: Akarian Irenhour
imageAlt: Akarian Irenhour, a long-haired elven warrior carrying a sword in a mountain forest
imageCaption: Akarian Irenhour — warrior and Guardian of Gael.
dek: A hunter and Guardian of Gael whose defense of heritage becomes a vigil, a duty to teach and a struggle to accept help amid loss.

facts.Record: Relic trial and selected later scenes; fuller history unresolved
facts.Name: Akarian Irenhour
facts.Early identity: Half-elf; calls himself a hunter and defender of cultural heritage

body:
Akarian Irenhour arrives as a wary half-elf who calls himself a hunter and a defender of his people’s culture. His later life as Gael’s Guardian brings a harder vigil, the training of companions and practical care under pressure. His first questions about Death and unfamiliar companions remain part of that history, even after he takes on the Guardian’s duties.

March 2024 · a hunter learning whom to trust

The March arrival scene describes a young half-elf landing through the portal and studying the strangers around him. He introduces himself as Akarian of the Irenhour. At first, the command to fight Death puzzles him: he understands ordinary death as part of life. Rolen, Claire and Jako explain the threat as they understand it.

Akarian says that his mother was human and that honour, rather than age alone, defines the elven heritage he wants to preserve. He calls himself a hunter with little experience fighting undead. When Claire describes raising a daughter of mixed heritage, he offers to help teach her. The offer is recorded; a completed course of teaching is not.

Jako shares remembered experiences through spores, but the account remains Jako’s perspective. Akarian asks whether he can trust such different companions. Before he teaches others, he has his own decisions to make about working with them.

Guardian of Gael

Gael is still recovering from Wrath, with living centers such as Hope and Stake surrounded by ruins, trials, cult activity, fiendish remnants, and unfinished infrastructure. As Guardian, Akarian has continuing duties in a region whose troubles did not end with that battle.

A practical warrior

The surviving synthesis describes Akarian as practical, joining his martial competence to the care of Gael. It supplies no basis for a complete account of his tactics or motives; those limits remain alongside his established Guardian role.

September 2024 · witnessing devotion

When he joins Dale and Saray in the Plains, Akarian looks hardened and ready for war. He says that he recognized his own unreadiness after arriving and prepared himself. His explanation of vigilance remains his account of the obligation he has taken on.

Dale asks him to witness an oath of devotion to Saray. Akarian accepts, stands with his sword and approves the promise. Alongside his combat trials, he witnesses and solemnly recognizes another person’s chosen commitment.

After the fighting, he urges a return so they can prepare for tomorrow, then offers a quiet “Well done.” His pressure to improve and his recognition of shared effort belong in the same history.

October 2024 · grief beneath the vigil

Akarian’s trial follows the loss of Nienna. When Elenia approaches him, he holds back a painful response and returns to the work at hand. His account connects the loss with his vigil, but his later actions should not all be reduced to a single wound.

He says he and Huoth have drawn essence from Hope and fashioned powerful relics. The claim establishes their role in this particular trial’s preparation; it is not a universal rule that every form of hope can be extracted or owned.

October 2024 · a lesson aimed at particular weaknesses

The paired trial makes Dale and Saray confront threats to their ability to protect one another. The narrator explicitly identifies their over-care for each other, reliance on blindsight and lack of an answer to hostile spellcasting as the weaknesses Akarian targeted. At the end, Akarian enters, lays his hands on them and gently brings them out.

This is a staged lesson, distinct from the later expeditions on Babel-Ashur. Its outcome does not establish either participant’s death. It complements the trial of responsibility described below: the preparation includes recognizing limits, not simply proving strength.

Responsibility, not only ability

Akarian divides the participants by the qualities he sees in them: Dale and Saray as devotion, Adelia and Scribonia as wisdom and logic, Elenia and Draygar as wildfire and passion. These are his judgments, not fixed descriptions of who those people must always be.

He places two rings at the center and allows negotiation, leaving them or fighting over them. What the participants choose is part of the test. When the dispute resolves, he tells Draygar to give Elenia the rings. His insistence that the question concerns responsibility, rather than ability, makes inheritance a decision about what people will do with power.

January 2025 · accepting help in a changed landscape

Gartina greets his renewed presence with surprise. Akarian credits Elenia’s persistence; his account of hearing prayers does not provide the missing scene or exact means of his return. The reunion should not be used to invent a resurrection spell.

They disagree about the sources and meaning of power, yet he acknowledges Gartina’s results and welcomes her company in the Plains. He insists that he is the weapon rather than his equipment, but still asks what her offered stones can do. Pride in his training coexists with accepting help.

Gartina draws his attention to the restored trees. He sees the life with his eyes while saying that his heart still perceives death. That is his emotional response, not evidence that the forest has disappeared or that Gael’s renewal failed.

April 2025 · a damaged certainty

Later trials complicate the composed steward. Akarian describes himself as no longer fully himself and asks for Saray’s wedding memory to be restored. He accepts a companion’s argument, fights with attention to his training and offers to take Sildithas’s watches so that another person can rest.

His remark that pressing forward is foolish occurs amid confusion about what is real. It does not establish a permanent doctrine of retreat: he also pushes ahead and eventually holds a discovered bridge for the others. The record preserves caution, anger and practical help together.

July 2026 · admitting a limit

During later work involving the tree, he admits that he cannot understand how ordinary magic could accomplish what is being asked. When another explanation is offered, he calls his own problem rust. The word may be self-deprecation; it is not a diagnosis of physical, emotional or spiritual decline.

The exact mechanics of Hope’s relics, the complete history of his relationship with Nienna and his later responsibilities remain open. His Guardian role and practical work endure alongside those gaps.

Scenes in sequence

These selected scenes preserve what was knowable when people acted. Dates below identify source postings in UTC; they do not supply an in-world calendar. A later appearance does not settle present status.

  1. 2024-03-24 · compatible RP

    A newcomer offers to preserve another child’s heritage

    Akarian introduces himself as a hunter and offers to help Claire teach her daughter about her elven heritage.

    Known at this stage
    He is still learning what the local struggle and cooperation require.
    Consequence
    His commitment to cultural continuity begins before the later Guardian role.
    Still unresolved
    No completed teaching arrangement or complete early biography is established.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6 · Receipt 7 · Receipt 8

  2. 2024-09-18 · compatible RP

    Standing witness to Dale’s choice

    Akarian witnesses Dale’s oath of devotion to Saray, then joins them in the field.

    Known at this stage
    The oath is Dale’s chosen commitment rather than an identity imposed by the teacher.
    Consequence
    Recognition and preparation form part of Akarian’s care for companions.
    Still unresolved
    The scene does not give him ownership of their choices.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6 · Receipt 7 · Receipt 8

  3. 2024-10-12 · quest

    Grief beneath the vigil

    Akarian describes making relics with Huoth and calls the company to a test.

    Known at this stage
    He speaks as a grieving guardian preparing others for a confrontation.
    Consequence
    The trial gives grief a practical expression in shared preparation.
    Still unresolved
    His description of the relics’ making remains his account.

    Receipt 1

  4. 2024-10-12 · quest

    A trial targets limits and ends with care

    The narrator identifies the particular weaknesses in Dale and Saray’s training; Akarian then gently brings them out.

    Known at this stage
    This is a staged paired trial.
    Consequence
    Learning requires more than confidence in protecting a loved one.
    Still unresolved
    The encounter is not a recorded expedition death or a Babel journey.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2

  5. 2024-10-12 · quest

    An outcome of the test

    Akarian directs Draygar to give Elenia the rings.

    Known at this stage
    The instruction follows the participants’ choices during the trial.
    Consequence
    The judgment belongs with the full scene, including Dale and Saray’s devotion.
    Still unresolved
    It does not establish permanent ownership of every relic.

    Receipt 1

  6. 2025-01-07 · compatible RP

    Accepting company without sharing every belief

    Akarian debates power with Gartina, acknowledges her results and accepts her company and help.

    Known at this stage
    The landscape has living trees even though it feels haunted by loss to him.
    Consequence
    Disagreement does not prevent practical cooperation.
    Still unresolved
    His renewed appearance and recollections do not name an exact return spell.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6 · Receipt 7 · Receipt 8

  7. 2025-04-17 · quest

    Care and forward pressure coexist

    Akarian offers to take Sildithas’s watches, then agrees to push on.

    Known at this stage
    The party is negotiating rest and urgency.
    Consequence
    His practical care remains visible beside the pressure to continue.
    Still unresolved
    A single exchange does not establish an inflexible doctrine of advance or retreat.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2
